story.originalTitle: Antonelli: I couldn’t see through my tears on title-clinching lap
story.summaryEn: Antonelli said he could not see through his tears on the final lap of the Mexico City Grand Prix, where he finished third to become Formula 1 world champion for the first time.
detailZh: 安东内利成为F1世界冠军：这位梅赛德斯车手表示，在墨西哥城大奖赛最后一圈他泪流满面，看不清赛道。
安东内利透露，在墨西哥城大奖赛的最后阶段他情绪难以自持，他在这场比赛中以第三名完赛，锁定2026年F1车手世界冠军；天空体育F1将从本周五起直播圣保罗大奖赛的各节练习与排位。
安东内利回看了一段视频集锦，回顾他从卡丁车到成为F1最年轻冠军的历程。
安东内利表示，在墨西哥城大奖赛最后一圈他“看不清”赛道，因为他在首次成为F1世界冠军之前情绪激动、泪流满面。
安东内利以第三名完赛，排在分站冠军马克斯·维斯塔潘和法拉利车手刘易斯·汉密尔顿之后，将塞巴斯蒂安·维特尔作为F1最年轻世界冠军的纪录提前了三年多，以20岁68天的年龄锁定总冠军。
这位意大利车手在车队无线电和赛后多次采访中情绪激动，并透露他在比赛最后阶段就已经哭了。

安东内利说：“其实在前一圈，我就大概损失了两秒，因为我基本上已经在哭了。我根本看不清前方。”
“我带着泪水，不知怎么地还能看到两辆法拉利。所以，那非常特别。那一刻，很多回忆涌上心头，从卡丁车一直到这里的全部记忆。”
“那是一个非常特别的最后一圈，而且毫无疑问，当我冲过终点线时，我彻底释放了情绪，因为我刚刚实现了自己最大的梦想之一。那非常特别。”
基米·安东内利，梅赛德斯 - 20岁68天（2026年）
塞巴斯蒂安·维特尔，红牛车队——23岁134天（2010年）
刘易斯·汉密尔顿，迈凯伦车队——23岁300天（2008年）
费尔南多·阿隆索，雷诺车队——24岁58天（2005年）
马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队——24岁73天（2021年）
基米·安东内利在墨西哥城大奖赛获得第三名后，成为有史以来最年轻的一级方程式世界冠军。
安东内利只是第三位赢得F1车手总冠军的意大利车手，也是自1953年阿尔贝托·阿斯卡里以来的第一位。
这位梅赛德斯车手在领奖台上被维斯塔潘和汉密尔顿举起，背景中播放着标志性的意大利歌曲《今夜无人入睡》和《Sarà, perché ti amo》，安东内利后来透露，这让他想起了已故的祖父。
“第一首歌对我来说非常感人，因为那是祖父过去常听的歌，所以听到它非常特别。我想他会非常骄傲，”安东内利在赛后新闻发布会上泪流满面，稍作平复后说道。
“天哪，我今天哭得太多了，但这是好事。我只是因为我的祖父而非常激动。”
基米·安东内利在成为有史以来最年轻的一级方程式世界冠军后心情大好。
安东内利：我会把与维斯塔潘和汉密尔顿同登领奖台的照片挂在家里
安东内利紧随F1最伟大的两位车手维斯塔潘和汉密尔顿之后完赛，从而成为世界冠军，这多少有些恰如其分。
安东内利在汉密尔顿于2025年令人震惊地转投法拉利后，接替了后者在梅赛德斯的位置，这位20岁的车手表示，能与两位多次获得世界冠军的车手一同登上领奖台，是一个“不可思议”的时刻。
“今年早些时候在加拿大也发生过同样的事，但显然这次很特别。我一定会把这张照片装裱起来挂在家里，因为这实在是一个不可思议的时刻，”他说。
“能看到两位书写了这项运动历史的了不起的车手展现出如此多的尊重，真的很特别，这是一个将永存、将永远被铭记的时刻。所以我一定会把这张照片装裱起来，挂在我家的墙上，这样每次进屋都能看得清清楚楚。”
前世界冠军马克斯·维斯塔潘和刘易斯·汉密尔顿在墨西哥将F1最新冠军基米·安东内利扛在肩上
安东内利从12岁起就是梅赛德斯的一员，自从他在2025年初完成F1首秀以来，他的父亲马尔科·安东内利几乎每场比赛都陪伴在他身边。
马尔科拥有一支拉力车队，但他在周六上午与基米的妹妹一起飞抵墨西哥，以确保他们能见证基米成为冠军。
安东内利说：“他们能来这里付出了很大努力，我非常高兴能够一起分享并见证这一刻，因为我的家人为我做出了、并且仍在做出难以置信的巨大牺牲。”
“尤其是我的父亲，尽管他自己的工作非常繁忙，他今年基本上每场比赛都来了。所以，你知道，拥有这样一位人物一直至关重要。
“他是那个让我保持脚踏实地的人，尤其是在非常高峰的时刻之后，但同样，他也是在我面临困难局面时、或者在一节练习或比赛前感觉不在最佳状态时始终陪伴在我身边的人。”
梅赛德斯车队领队托托·沃尔夫在基米·安东内利成为一级方程式历史上最年轻的冠军后欣喜若狂。
“然后，当然，梅赛德斯，我怎么感谢他们都不为过，因为首先，他们是在我11岁时冒险押注我的人，他们一直相信我，现在依然如此。”
“首先，能为这支车队比赛，是一种巨大的荣幸。希望我们在未来几年能取得更多成功。”
"但同样，能跟博诺（安东内利的比赛工程师彼得·博宁顿）以及所有其他人、所有那些总是来到赛道并竭尽全力的男孩女孩们共事，也是一大荣幸，因为这是一个不可思议的团队，一个非常独特、非常团结的团队。他们每一个人都在实现这一目标的过程中发挥了巨大的作用。"

detailEn: Kimi Antonelli becomes F1 world champion: Mercedes driver says he couldn't see through his tears on final lap of Mexico City GP

Kimi Antonelli has revealed he was overcome with emotion during the closing stages of the Mexico City Grand Prix, which he finished third in to seal the 2026 F1 Drivers' Championship; watch every session of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1
Kimi Antonelli watches back a montage of videos from his journey from go-karting, to F1's youngest champion
Kimi Antonelli says he "couldn't see" through his tears on the final lap of the Mexico City Grand Prix as he was overcome with emotion before becoming Formula 1 world champion for the first time.

Antonelli finished third behind race-winner Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton to lower Sebastian Vettel's record of being F1's youngest world champion by over three years, sealing the title at 20 years and 68 days old.
The Italian was overcome with emotion on team radio and in several post-race interviews, and revealed he was already crying during the closing stages of the race.

"Already the lap before, I think I lost probably two seconds because I was already crying, basically. I couldn't see clearly ahead," said Antonelli.
"I could see two Ferraris somehow with the tears. So, it was very special. A lot of memories went through my mind in that moment, all the memories since karting all the way to here.
"It was a very special final lap, and definitely, when I crossed the line, I let it all out because it was just achieving one of my biggest dreams. It was very special."
Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes - 20 years and 68 days (2026)
Sebastian Vettel, Red Bull - 23 years and 134 days (2010)
Lewis Hamilton, McLaren - 23 years and 300 days (2008)
Fernando Alonso,, Renault - 24 years and 58 days (2005)
Max Verstappen, Red Bull - 24 years and 73 days (2021)
Kimi Antonelli became the youngest ever Formula 1 world champion after finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix
Antonelli is just the third Italian driver to win the F1 Drivers' Championship and the first since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

The Mercedes driver was lifted up by Verstappen and Hamilton on the podium with iconic Italian songs 'Nessun Dorma' and 'Sarà, perché ti amo' playing in the background, which Antonelli later revealed made him think about his late grandfather.

"The first song was very emotional for me because it was a song that my grandfather used to listen to always, so it was very special to hear that. I think he would be very proud," said Antonelli as he took a moment to compose himself through the tears in the post-race press conference.
"Oh my God, I've cried way too much today, but it's good. I just got very emotional because of my grandfather."
Kimi Antonelli was in buoyant mood after becoming the youngest ever Formula 1 world champion.
Antonelli: I will put podium picture with Verstappen-Hamilton in my house
It was somewhat fitting that Antonelli followed home two of F1's greatest drivers in Verstappen and Hamilton to become world champion.

Antonelli replaced Hamilton at Mercedes following the latter's shock move to Ferrari in 2025 and the 20-year-old says it was an "incredible" moment to share the podium with the two multiple world champions.

"It happened in Canada as well this year, earlier in the year, but obviously this is special. I will definitely frame the picture and put it in my house because it's just an incredible moment," he said.

"To see so much respect from two incredible drivers who have done the history of the sport is truly special, and a moment that will live and will always be remembered. So definitely I will frame the picture and put it on the wall of my house so I can see it very well whenever I go in."
Former World champions Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton lift F1's newest champion, Kimi Antonelli, onto their shoulders in Mexico
Antonelli has been part of Mercedes since he was 12 years old and his father, Marco Antonelli, has been by his side at nearly every race since he made his F1 debut at the start of 2025.
Marco has a rallying team but flew into Mexico on Saturday morning with Kimi's sister to ensure they could watch Kimi become champion.

"It was a big effort for them to come here, and I'm very happy to be able to share and witness this moment altogether because my family has made, and they still do, an incredible amount of sacrifices for me," said Antonelli.
"Especially my dad, he has come to basically all the races this year, despite being very busy with his own work, his own job. So, you know, that has been crucial, to have such a figure.

"He was the one keeping me grounded, especially after very high moments, but as well he was the one that was always there when I was facing a difficult situation, or I wasn't feeling the best ahead of a session or ahead of the race.
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff was ecstatic after Kimi Antonelli became the youngest ever champion in Formula 1 history.

"Then, of course, Mercedes, I couldn't thank them enough because, first of all, they were the ones who took the gamble when I was 11, and they were the ones who believed in me all the way, and they still do.
"t's been a massive privilege to be able to, first of all, race for this team. Hopefully we'll have much more success in the upcoming years.

"But as well, it's been a big privilege to work with Bono (Antonelli's race engineer Peter Bonnington) and with all the other guys, all the other boys and girls who always come to the track and do their best, because it's an incredible group, a very unique one and a very united one. And every single one of them has played a massive role in achieving this."

detailZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿：法拉利车队的七届F1世界冠军在访问拉法口岸后，呼吁以色列“放行援助卡车”进入加沙。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿周二访问了拉法口岸，实地了解向加沙运送援助物资的工作；这位法拉利车手周三在Instagram发帖，呼吁以色列“履行停火协议下的义务”。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿在访问拉法口岸后，呼吁以色列“放行援助卡车”进入加沙。
汉密尔顿周二在埃及，实地了解向加沙运送人道主义与救援物资的工作。这位法拉利车手还参观了拉法口岸，并走访了埃及红新月会的援助仓库。
美国支持的以色列与哈马斯之间的停火协议仍然有效，但并未结束以色列对加沙的打击，同时联合国世界粮食计划署表示，加沙三分之二的人口难以获得足够的食物。
汉密尔顿此前曾呼吁该地区实现和平，他表示援助物资因“疯狂的理由”被拒绝进入加沙。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿（@lewishamilton）分享的一条帖子。

这位七届世界冠军在Instagram上发文称：“过去三年以色列在加沙的种族灭绝行径令人震惊。”
“人们被剥夺自由、安全和尊严，这是不公正的。任何人都不应被当作生命不那么重要来对待。”
“我看到绵延数英里的围墙，是为了把他们困在里面而建的。站在外面，感觉就像一座露天监狱，我满脑子想的都是进去帮忙。”
“在拉法口岸，我看到食品卡车排着队准备出发，但它们经常不被允许进入，或者面临严重延误。我交谈过的排在第一位的那位司机已经等了超过12个小时。”
在附近的物流中心，我看到了救援人员的辛勤工作，但我也看到了因荒唐理由被拒绝的物资。睡袋、急救包、医疗设备、轮椅，甚至给孩子们的足球。
以色列需要履行停火协议下的义务，让援助卡车进入。没有任何借口。
我知道很多人都感受到同样的无助。同样觉得需要做点什么，而不是袖手旁观。我不想让我们对他们的苦难习以为常。我不想让我们移开视线。
周三，以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡否认以色列在拖延物资进入加沙，并将加沙不断恶化的状况归咎于哈马斯，指责他们拒绝解除武装并截留援助物资用于军事用途。
2021年，汉密尔顿创立了Mission 44慈善机构，旨在支持年轻人并改善他们获得教育和就业机会的途径。
他还支持了人道主义和救援倡议，以及为受冲突影响的人们提供帮助的努力。
汉密尔顿是在上周末参加圣保罗大奖赛并获得第九名后进行了此次访问。他接下来将代表法拉利参加拉斯维加斯大奖赛，第一次练习赛于11月20日星期五举行。
汉密尔顿分享了与加沙儿童会面的细节
在首次发帖一天后，汉密尔顿于周四再次通过社交媒体分享了他与从加沙撤离的儿童互动的细节。
除了分享一组自己与孩子们的合影外，汉密尔顿写道：“在埃及见到一些由@inaraorg支持的从加沙撤离的巴勒斯坦儿童，我的心都碎了。
“这些美丽、聪明的孩子经历了创伤、悲痛和可怕的伤害，这些是任何孩子都不应该承受的事情。有些孩子在袭击中中弹或严重烧伤，仍在面对复杂的康复之路。但真正打动我的是他们如此坚韧，而且似乎在彼此身上找到了许多快乐。

“当我问起他们的梦想时，他们谈到想成为老师和医生，这样就能像曾经帮助过他们的人那样去帮助别人。在经历了这一切之后，他们仍然想象着一个关爱他人的未来。这让我一直难以忘怀。
“我在学校、医院和一家心理健康诊所遇到了孩子们，帮助他们走出创伤。我还走进了一些家庭，倾听他们关于康复以及与亲人——他们的孩子、父母、兄弟姐妹——分离的故事。那种分离和不确定带来的痛苦令人难以理解。
“他们的故事让我想到了仍留在加沙的孩子们，他们生活在恶劣的条件下。据报道，自2023年10月以来，已有超过21500名儿童丧生，45000人受伤。他们每一个人都曾有过一个家和一个未来。我们不能忘记他们。
“这些孩子和你们的孩子没有不同。他们的生命同样珍贵。他们本应能在教室里与朋友相伴感到安全，与家人在一起，并憧憬未来。我非常感激我遇到的年轻人正在获得他们所需的帮助，但他们不得不离开家园去寻找安全，这令人心碎。”
加沙卫生当局表示，自2023年10月以色列开始对加沙发动攻势以来，已有超过74000人丧生。

detailEn: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari's seven-time F1 world champion urges Israel to 'let the aid trucks in' to Gaza after visit to Rafah border

Lewis Hamilton visited the Rafah border on Tuesday to witness efforts to transport aid into Gaza; Ferrari driver published Instagram post on Wednesday calling on Israel to "fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire"
Lewis Hamilton urged Israel to "let the aid trucks in" to Gaza after visiting the Rafah border.

Hamilton was in Egypt on Tuesday to witness efforts to deliver humanitarian and relief aid bound for Gaza. The Ferrari driver also toured the Rafah border crossing and visited the Egyptian Red Crescent's aid warehouses.

The US-backed ceasefire between Israel and Hamas remains in place but has not ended Israeli strikes on Gaza, while the UN World Food Programme says two-thirds of Gaza's population are struggling to get enough to eat.
Hamilton - who has previously called for peace in the region - said aid was being denied entry into Gaza for "crazy reasons".

The seven-time world champion posted on Instagram: "The past three years of Israel's genocide in Gaza is appalling.
"It's an injustice for people to be denied their freedom, their safety and their dignity. No human being should be treated as though their life matters less.
"I saw walls stretching for miles, built to keep them in. Standing there, outside what felt like an open-air prison, all I could think about was getting in to help.
"At Rafah border, I saw food trucks lined up ready to go, but they're regularly not allowed in or face major delays. The first driver in line that I spoke to had already been waiting over 12 hours.

"At the nearby logistics centre, I saw the hard work of the aid workers, but I also saw what gets rejected for crazy reasons. Sleeping bags, first-aid kits, medical equipment, wheelchairs, even footballs for kids.
"Israel needs to fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire and let the aid trucks in. No excuse.
"I know so many people feel that same helplessness. That same need to do something rather than just watch. I don't want us to get used to their suffering. I don't want us to look away."

On Wednesday, Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli Prime Minister, denied Israel was delaying the entry of supplies into Gaza, and blamed Hamas for the worsening conditions in Gaza, accusing them of a refusal to disarm and seizing aid for military use.
In 2021, Hamilton founded Mission 44, a charity aimed at supporting young people and improving ⁠access to education and employment ​opportunities.
He has also backed ​humanitarian and relief initiatives, and ​efforts to support people affected by ⁠conflict.
Hamilton made his visit after competing in the Sao Paulo GP last weekend, where he finished ninth. He will next compete for Ferrari in the Las Vegas GP, with Practice 1 on Friday November 20.
Hamilton shares details of meeting children from Gaza
A day after his initial post, Hamilton took to social media again on Thursday to share details of his interactions with children he met who have been evacuated from Gaza.

Along with sharing a selection of photos of himself with the children, Hamilton wrote: "Meeting some of the Palestinian children evacuated from Gaza and supported by @inaraorg in Egypt broke my heart.

"Beautiful, bright children who have faced trauma, grief and horrendous injuries, things no child should ever have to endure. Some have been shot or badly burned in attacks and are still facing a complicated road towards recovery. But what really struck me was how resilient they were and how much joy they seem to find in each other.

"When I asked about their dreams, they spoke about becoming teachers and doctors so they could help others, the way they were helped. After everything they've been through, they still imagine a future caring for other people. That has stayed with me.

"I met children at school, in hospital and at a mental health clinic helping them work through their trauma. I also went into families' homes and listened to their stories of recovery and being separated from loved ones - their children, their parents, their siblings. The pain of that separation and uncertainty is hard to comprehend.

"Their stories made me think about the children still in Gaza, who are living in terrible conditions. According to reports, more than 21,500 children have been killed and 45,000 injured since October 2023. Every one of them had a home and a future. We can't forget them.

"These children are no different from yours. Their lives are just as precious. They should be able to feel safe in a classroom with friends, be with their families and imagine a future. I'm so grateful the young people I met are getting the help they need, but it's heartbreaking that they've had to leave their homes to find safety."
Gaza health authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed since Israel began its Gaza assault in October 2023.
Israel launched the offensive after Hamas gunmen led an attack on southern Israel, which it said killed around 1,200.
